multiScaleR model selection

Source: R/aic_tab.R
bic_tab.Rd

Creates a model selection table ranked by BIC for a list of fitted models. Mixed lists containing both multiScaleR objects and plain model objects are supported.

Usage

bic_tab(mod_list,
        mod_names = NULL,
        verbose = FALSE,
        ...)

Arguments

mod_list

List containing fitted multiScaleR objects (from multiScale_optim) and/or plain fitted model objects. All models must have been fit to the same number of observations.

mod_names

Optional character vector of model names. Length must equal length(mod_list). By default, names are constructed as [kernel]right-hand-side-formula for multiScaleR objects.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, the table is also printed to the console. Default: FALSE.

...

Additional arguments (not used).

Value

A data frame of class "bictab" (from the AICcmodavg package) sorted by ascending BIC, containing:

Modnames

Model name.

K

Number of fitted likelihood parameters, including ancillary parameters such as negative-binomial dispersion, plus optimized scale and shape parameters for multiScaleR models.

BIC

Bayesian information criterion value.

Delta_BIC

Difference from the top model.

BICWt

BIC weight.

Cum.Wt

Cumulative BIC weight.

LL

Log-likelihood.

Details

The table is constructed using bictabCustom from the AICcmodavg package. BIC penalizes model complexity more heavily than AIC as sample size grows, and is often preferred when the goal is identifying the single best-supported model rather than model averaging. Sigma (and shape for "expow") is counted in K. Fitted parameter counts and log-likelihood validation follow aic_tab, including all estimated components of unmarked models.

Author

Bill Peterman

Examples

## Simulate data
set.seed(555)

points <- vect(cbind(c(5,7,9,11,13),
                     c(13,11,9,7,5)))

mat_list <- list(r1 = rast(matrix(rnorm(20^2),
                                  nrow = 20)),
                 r2 = rast(matrix(rnorm(20^2),
                                  nrow = 20)))
rast_stack <- rast(mat_list)
kernel_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = points,
                             raster_stack = rast_stack,
                             max_D = 5,
                             kernel = 'gaussian',
                             sigma = NULL)
#> 
#> No sigma values provided...
#> Creating necessary elements to optimize sigma
#> 
#> Extracting values from raster layers...
## Example response data
y <- rnorm(5)

## Create data frame with raster variables
dat <- data.frame(y = y,
                  kernel_inputs$kernel_dat)
mod1 <- glm(y ~ r1,
            data = dat)
mod2 <- glm(y ~ r2,
            data = dat)
mod3 <- glm(y ~ r1 + r2,
            data = dat)

## NOTE: This code is only for demonstration
## Optimization results will have no meaning

opt_mod1 <- multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = mod1,
                             kernel_inputs = kernel_inputs,
                             par = NULL,
                             n_cores = NULL)
#> 
#> 
#> Optimization complete
#> 
#>  WARNING!!!
#>  The estimated scale of effect approaches or exceeds the current search extent.
#>  Consider increasing max_D in `kernel_prep` to >=11.9 to ensure accurate estimation of scale.
#> 
#> 
#>  WARNING!!!
#>  The standard error of one or more `sigma` estimates is >= 50% of the estimated mean value.
#>  Carefully assess whether or not this variable is meaningful in your analysis and interpret with caution.
#> 
#> 

opt_mod2 <- multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = mod2,
                             kernel_inputs = kernel_inputs,
                             par = NULL,
                             n_cores = NULL)
#> 
#> 
#> Optimization complete
#> 
#>  WARNING!!!
#>  The estimated scale of effect approaches or exceeds the current search extent.
#>  Consider increasing max_D in `kernel_prep` to >=16.44 to ensure accurate estimation of scale.
#> 
#> 
#>  WARNING!!!
#>  The standard error of one or more `sigma` estimates is >= 50% of the estimated mean value.
#>  Carefully assess whether or not this variable is meaningful in your analysis and interpret with caution.
#> 
#> 
opt_mod3 <- multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = mod3,
                             kernel_inputs = kernel_inputs,
                             par = NULL,
                             n_cores = NULL)
#> 
#> 
#> Optimization complete
#> 
#>  WARNING!!!
#>  The estimated scale of effect approaches or exceeds the current search extent.
#>  Consider increasing max_D in `kernel_prep` to >=16.44 to ensure accurate estimation of scale.
#> 
#> 

 ## BIC table
 mod_list <- list(opt_mod1, opt_mod2, opt_mod3)

 bic_tab(mod_list = mod_list)
#> 
#> Model selection based on BIC:
#> 
#>                     K   BIC Delta_BIC BICWt Cum.Wt    LL
#> [gaussian]~ r1 + r2 6  3.26      0.00  0.98   0.98  3.20
#> [gaussian]~ r2      4 11.56      8.30  0.02   0.99 -2.56
#> [gaussian]~ r1      4 13.41     10.15  0.01   1.00 -3.49
#> 

 ## BIC table with specified names
 bic_tab(mod_list = mod_list,
         mod_names = c('mod1', 'mod2', 'mod3'))
#> 
#> Model selection based on BIC:
#> 
#>      K   BIC Delta_BIC BICWt Cum.Wt    LL
#> mod3 6  3.26      0.00  0.98   0.98  3.20
#> mod2 4 11.56      8.30  0.02   0.99 -2.56
#> mod1 4 13.41     10.15  0.01   1.00 -3.49
#>
